problem: Object navigation only asks agents to reach a named object, but real users state a task goal (e.g. 'heat bread') that can be satisfied at places combining several tool objects. Prior object-relation or affordance-landscape methods do not explicitly link affordances to the objects and places that provide them.
motivation: Finding a place that affords a function is more practical than finding a specific tool, but it is harder because the target descriptions are abstract and the tools are diverse. The paper observes that affordances depend on relations between manipulations, target objects and tool objects, and that these relations can be mined automatically from simulator interactions.
key_idea: Build an Object-to-Manipulation Graph (manipulation, tool-object and target-object nodes, edges from co-occurrence and interaction) and refine it with a GCN to give an A3C navigation policy affordance-aware features.
insight: Explicitly modelling affordance-object relations gives large gains over a plain RGB+goal baseline. In the ablation, the graph embedding alone reaches SR 37.0 and the affordance embedding alone 38.8, versus 28.0 for RGB only. Using both reaches 42.0, so the two features are complementary. Gains are largest on the hard L>=5 episodes and on affordances needing several tools (Heat SR 35.0 vs 16.0 baseline).
method: Task and dataset: affordance navigation in AI2-THOR. The goal is a (manipulation, target object) pair, e.g. 'heat bread'. There are 200 affordances across 5 types (Heat, Cool, Wash, Put, Store). Ground-truth target places are auto-annotated by running a PDDL planner at every reachable location and keeping places where the plan executes successfully.

OMG graph structure: three node types (manipulation, tool object, target object) and two edge types. Manipulation-tool edges come from a normalized co-occurrence matrix over dataset target places. Target-tool edges are binary and set to 1 if the target can successfully interact with the tool in the simulator.

Manipulation node: a ResNet-18 classifier over the RGB view predicts a manipulation probability P, trained with labels propagated to frames near successful places. The visual vector is the last-layer feature re-weighted by P, concatenated with a GloVe embedding.

Tool object node: a Faster R-CNN (COCO pre-trained, fine-tuned on 3x10^4 AI2-THOR images) detects tool categories. The node feature is box position plus appearance feature plus GloVe, and is all zeros when the tool is not detected. Target object nodes use zero visual vectors plus GloVe, to avoid bias from target-object occurrence.

GCN optimization: a 3-layer GCN (1024, 1024, 512 dims) runs on the binary adjacency. Outputs are an affordance embedding (from the manipulation and target node features) and a |V|-dim graph embedding (one value aggregated per node).

Policy network: GloVe semantic branch, affordance embedding, graph embedding and RGB feature are fused and fed into A3C with a 512-D hidden layer. Reward is 5 for Done at the nearest target place, 4 at another target place, and -0.01 per step otherwise.

setting.backbone: A3C policy with 3-layer GCN, ResNet-18 manipulation classifier and Faster R-CNN detector (trained; no pre-trained LLM)
setting.training_data: RL in AI2-THOR training FloorPlans, 12 asynchronous agents for 3M episodes; Faster R-CNN pre-trained on COCO and fine-tuned on 3x10^4 AI2-THOR images; self-collected affordance dataset (200 affordances)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookUp, LookDown, Done
setting.privileged: none at test time (graph relations come from training data and simulator interaction; GT is used only for training reward and labels)

numbers.backbone: A3C + GCN OMG + ResNet-18 + Faster R-CNN
numbers.extra: 200 affordances; ALL = all episodes; also L>=5 SR 28.6 / SPL 19.6
Phase 1: target object navigation; Phase 2: affordance navigation; success within 1.5 m

numbers_note: The benchmark is newly introduced (AI2-THOR affordance navigation); the paper does not name official splits, so 'test' is used for its unseen-environment evaluation.
results: On the new benchmark the OMG agent reaches SR 42.0 / SPL 27.8, beating the BASELINE (28.0 / 16.1, +14.0 SR and +11.7 SPL) and the adapted ObjNavigation (28.8 / 16.9) and IntExp (29.8 / 18.0). Gains are larger on L>=5 episodes (SR 28.6 vs 13.7 best baseline). A real-robot test gives 72.0% SR in phase 1 and 37.0% in phase 2.
limitations: The target affordance (target object plus manipulation) is given, and the task is limited to affordances of a target object; open-ended affordances are not handled.
Only five affordance types in AI2-THOR are covered, and the tool detector plus relation graph depend on predefined tool categories.
Real-world success in the affordance phase is low (37%), and the real-world test is a small simplified setup.
